pattern: Serial accumulator chain and priority mux cascade
strategy: Rebalance into tree for fast domain; flatten priority select to 5-level encoder tree
rationale: Reduces combinational depth from 7 to 3 levels in fast accumulator (3-level reduction); converts 24-stage priority mux to ~5 stages via balanced tree—eliminates ripple dependencies on critical path
target: acc[0..7] summation at lines 106-110; sel_chain cascade at lines 129-136
area_cost: small — rebalancing uses same gate count, priority tree adds ~10 mux cells for parallelism
equivalence_argument: Fast domain: tree computes (term[0]+term[1])+(term[2]+term[3])+...+(term[6]+term[7]) in parallel at level 0, then pairs of those at level 1, then final sum at level 2—addition is associative, so result matches sum[TAPS-1] bit-for-bit across all widths. Reset preserves zero state because all intermediate wires reset to 0. Slow domain: first_set[i] identifies the first set s_req bit using prefix-OR; balanced mux tree then selects its index. Only one first_set[i] can be high, so sel_chain[SEL] converges to that index's value. any_chain[SEL] = OR(all s_req bits) is unchanged. Reset clears all registers to 0; priority encoder returns 0 if no requests.
